text:
jen: heads-up — spike readout: attribution granularity vs billing windowing. thinking about whether we keep per-request token attribution or rollup earlier into minute windows for billing accuracy and cost savings.

mike: +1 we need the tradeoffs spelled out. per-request = perfect audit but huge write rate and storage. windowed = cheap but moves complexity to reconciliation.

kai: also depends on dedupe semantics. if we batch-attrib into windows we still need a way to map late arrivals back into the right customer/time bucket. watermarking?

sana: what are acceptable SLA bounds here? finance wants billed usage to be within 0.5% of true tokens daily. legal asks for auditability to trace a charged token to a request.

mike: proposal: keep ingest event model as-is (one event per request with tokens + attribution keys). Enrich and index into short-term windowed aggregates every 30s for fast billing estimates and quota enforcement. Persist raw events to tiered storage for audits and reconciles.

jen: that splits responsibilities nicely. quick enforcement from aggregates, truth from raw. But raw write rate is concerning. estimates? 500k req/s peak -> 20M events/min. storage ops pretty heavy.

kai: we can compress raw events by delta-encoding and deduping on client-side id. also consider probabilistic sampling for long term storage and keep full raw only for flagged/errored requests. sampling hurts full auditability though.

mike: another angle: adaptive granularity per customer tier. enterprise customers get full per-request raw retention; self-serve get windowed retention with sampled raw events. aligns with pricing and reduces infra burden.

sana: that's reasonable business-wise. we need a clear contract: minimum retention windows per tier, and an SLA for audit replays (e.g., enterprise: full replay within 24h; self-serve: replay possible from aggregates only).

jen: open question: how to reconcile late arrivals and duplicates? my thinking: attach an immutable provenance id to every request at the gateway. ingest de-duplicator keeps the highest-seen sequence per provenance id. final attribution job performs idempotent upserts keyed by provenance+window.

kai: pseudocode for upsert window job:
```
// ingest_event {provenance_id, customer_id, tokens, event_ts}
window = floor(event_ts / 300) // 5min windows
upsert key=(customer_id, window, provenance_id) -> keep max(tokens, existing)
aggregate by (customer_id, window) sum(tokens)
```
This keeps de-dupe and bounds the reconciliation to window keys.

mike: nice. but watch out for event_ts skew and clock untrustworthiness. prefer gateway-assigned ingestion_ts for windowing and keep event_ts as metadata. then reconciliation uses ingestion_ts watermark.

jen: agreed. watermark policy idea: watermark = max_ingest_ts - 2m. events arriving after watermark go into a late-arrivals queue processed with a separate reconciliation run that mutates window aggregates and emits audit corrections.

sana: finance wants corrections to be auditable. can we emit "billing_correction" events that include before/after token totals, affected windows, and provenance ids? Those get stored in the audit log and surfaced in console.

kai: yes — corrections should be explicit events. sample correction event format: `{"type":"billing_correction","customer":"C123","window":"2026-07-08T12:00Z","delta_tokens":-120,"provenance_ids":[...],"reason":"late_arrival"}`. store in append-only audit stream.

mike: one more operational concern: replay costs. If we keep full raw events we need efficient incremental re-aggregation. Suggest we store raw events partitioned by ingestion_day/customer and maintain per-partition checkpoints so replays only touch changed partitions.

jen: action items: 1) Kai draft an RFC with: ingestion provenance id, ingestion_ts windowing, watermark policy, late-arrival queue semantics, correction event schema, and tiered retention model. 2) Mike to run cost estimate for raw-event retention vs sampled retention across traffic profiles. 3) Sana to align finance/ops on correction SLAs.

billing-bot: deploy:reconciler v0.2 started for test cluster — logs: `reconciler: started, dry_run=true, target_day=2026-07-07` :rocket:

mike: thanks — will validate dry run output against sample dataset.

jen: cool. if no objections I'll put this on next week's eng-platform sync for sign-off. :thumbsup:

sana: +1

kai: will have RFC by EOW.
